source: User-provided alpine mountain and lake photograph, 1230 × 632.
prompts: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: bottom sky plate of a photorealistic website parallax scene. Edit target: attached alpine landscape photograph. Produce only the SKY BACKGROUND layer. Remove every mountain, forest, hillside, lake, grass and all land. Seamlessly inpaint the removed area with the same naturally pale blue daytime sky and subtle thin white clouds as the original upper sky. Preserve original sky colors and cloud placement in upper half, extend to the bottom. Same landscape composition and approximately 1230:632 aspect ratio, output 2460x1264 if possible. Full opaque photographic sky fills entire rectangular image edge to edge. No transparency, no new sun, no birds, no labels, no border, no text. This image will sit behind mountains cut from the reference.

Use case: background-extraction. Asset type: middle depth mountain plate for website parallax, transparent PNG. Edit target: attached alpine landscape photograph. Extract the entire distant snowy MOUNTAIN RANGE, preserving precisely the original three iconic snow-covered peaks, all mountain ridgeline positions, rock and snow textures, original perspective and original colors. Keep the mountain peaks at exactly their original normalized x,y coordinates. Remove ALL SKY above the mountain silhouette to actual alpha transparency. Replace the near dark forest, green slopes, lake and all foreground below the mountain range with a plausible continuation of the distant rock and alpine mountain foothills all the way down to bottom edge, so no transparent gaps occur BELOW the ridgeline when foreground moves. Preserve wide landscape canvas 1230:632 aspect ratio with original framing, output 2460x1264 if possible. The upper approximately 28% is fully transparent, irregular silhouette follows original peaks. Actual transparent alpha, no checkerboard pixels, no opaque black or white backdrop. No labels, text, border or restyling. Do not invent extra mountains or move peaks.

Use case: background-extraction. Asset type: foreground plate for website parallax, transparent PNG. Edit target: attached alpine landscape photograph. Precisely extract the whole FOREGROUND from the photo: the green hillside and tall trees beginning at the left edge around 44% image height, the dark evergreen forests across the middle, the green right hillside beginning at the right edge around 44% height, all closer grass, winding footpath, shoreline, entire lake with its original reflections, bottom edge stones, flowers and grass. Remove the sky and ALL distant snowy / rocky mountains above and behind the forest/hill silhouette to actual transparent alpha. Keep exact original normalized positions, geometry, framing, lighting and colors. Retain complete photo pixels BELOW the irregular foreground silhouette all the way to the bottom edge; lake reflections remain opaque and unchanged. Keep full wide canvas 1230:632 aspect ratio, output 2460x1264 if possible; do not crop or center the cutout. The scene's upper portion above original green hillside/forest horizon must be fully transparent. Actual transparent PNG alpha, no checkerboard pixels, no black or white backdrop. No labels, text, borders or restyling.
note: The generated plates are photographic reconstructions. The generation tool returned RGB checkerboard backgrounds, so SVG silhouettes mask them at render time. original.webp preserves the supplied photograph as the static fallback.
